sentence: To determine if an odd number can be written as the sum of two primes, note that if you use two odd primes then their sum is even.
sentence-category-reason: Explains parity reasoning that two odd primes sum to an even number.

sentence: Therefore, for an odd integer to be expressed as the sum of two primes, one of the primes must be 2.
sentence-category-reason: Deduction that one prime must be 2 for an odd sum.

sentence: In this case, the odd number n must equal 2 + p, where p is a prime number.
sentence-category-reason: Expresses the structural form n = 2 + p for odd n with p prime.

sentence: That means n can be expressed as the sum of two primes exactly when n − 2 is prime.
sentence-category-reason: States the equivalence condition that n − 2 must be prime.
